flagged.evidence: The page says the examples “check the right-coset sign convention.” But ex-qa-hidden-shift-dihedral-cosets identifies the equal-value classes as left cosets and concludes, “This convention uses left cosets,” explicitly noting that the displayed right coset is not the hidden left coset. The page summary mischaracterizes the convention illustrated.

alg-qa-finite-cyclic-discrete-logarithm specifies that D is found using “exact rational comparisons.” The theorem’s classical bit-cost bound has no term for the encoded size or processing cost of δ. For example, with δ = 2^(K−1)/(2^K+1), D = 2 and ln(1/δ) stays bounded as K grows, but determining D requires an exact comparison on K-bit integers. The stated bound therefore needs a δ input-length term or an explicit exclusion of this preprocessing cost.
